html:
China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) on 11 December 2001, after about fifteen years of talks.

To get in, China cut tariffs, opened banking and other services to foreign firms, and agreed to follow WTO rules. In return its exports gained steady access to the markets of the United States, Europe and the other members.

It capped two decades of reform and opening begun under Deng Xiaoping and tried out first in places like the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone. Foreign companies moved assembly to factories on China's coast, and China's exports grew about sixfold within a decade. It became "the workshop of the world", and in 2010 it passed Japan as the second largest economy.

The "China shock" also cost many factory jobs in the United States and Europe. Quarrels over subsidies and intellectual property grew, and led to the trade war that began in 2018.
sum: China joined the World Trade Organization (WTO) on 11 December 2001, after about fifteen years of talks.
